μελαίνω.definition: Medic., cause , Hp.Aph.5.20:—Pass., turn black, as a symptom of mortification, Id.Art.69, Fract.11

μελάμπυγος.definition: black-bottomed, considered a mark of; of a kind of eagle, v

μελαναίων.definition: the part of a ship covered with pitch, Ar.Fr.817

μελανόζυξ.definition: lit. black benched, i. e. manned with swarthy rowers, A.Supp.530

μελάνω.definition: intr., grow black, only in Il.7.64 . . , , cf. Arist.Pr.934a15; but Aristarch. read in the second clause and took trans., = , makes the sea black:—later writers use intr. , Thphr.Ign.50, A.R.4.1574, Arat.836; Call.Epi…

μελασμός.definition: blackening of flesh from mortification; dyeing black, Dsc.1.112, Gal.12.446

μέλδω.definition: soften by boiling, Call.Fr.309; Man.6.464:-Hom. only in Med. , . . , Il.21.363 :-Pass., Nic.Th.108

μελέτη.definition: care, attention, Hes.Op.412, Epich.[284]; Medic., treatment, Hp.Fract.31, 35 , Art.50

μελέτωρ.definition: one who cares for, an avenger, S.El.846

μέλημα.definition: object of care, beloved; care, anxiety, A.Eu.444, Theoc.14.2, etc

μελίζω.definition: fut. LXXLe.1.6: aor. D.H.7.72; Pass., have the limbs fully formed, Opp.l.c

μελίκηρα.definition: spawn of the murex, as being like a; gloss on , Gal.19.113

μελίπαις σίμβλος.definition: the hive with its honey-children, AP12.249

μελιτισμός.definition: Medic., treatment with honey, Mnesith. ap. Orib.inc.19.8

μελιτόω.definition: in Pass., to be sweetened with honey; to be filled with honey, Plu.2.628d

μελίφρων.definition: gen. sweet to the mind; Act., whose care is honey, A.R.4.1132

μελλησμός.definition: procrastination, indecision of; approach, threatening, of disease, Aret.SD1.11

μέλλω.definition: to be destined or likely to, indicating an estimated certainty or strong probability in the present, past, or future : a. c. pres. inf. , of a probability in the present, where belike the best are holding counsel, Il.…

μελοθεσία.definition: assignment of parts of the; of the Universe, position of its parts at the beginning of things, Paul.Al.T.2

μέλπω.definition: Il.1.474, Lasus1, etc.: Ep. impf; intr., sing, A.Ag.245, E.IT429 : c.acc.cogn., A.Ag.1445; E.Med.150, Tr.547 ; let it sound, Id.Ion881 : c. dat. instrum., play on . . , AP6.195 ; of the swan, Anacreont.58.9

μέλω.definition: Med. used in both voices, either in; by all manner of wiles am I in men's thoughts, i. e. am well known to them, Od.9.20; 12.70; Thgn.245; Pi.Fr.155; Id.O.10.14; E.Andr.850 ; . . Id.Tr.842; AP5.121 ; Them.Or.1.10a: pf…

μελῳδία.definition: singing, chanting, E.Rh.923, etc; chant, choral song, Pl.Lg.935e, cf. 812d; lullaby, ib.790e: generally, music, Phld.Mus.p.12 K

μενεαίνω.definition: desire earnestly or eagerly, c. pres; to be angry, rage, Il.19.68, 24.22,54; 19.58; rage against one, 15.104, Od.1.20, etc.; wrestled with death, Il.16.491 .—Ep., and Ps.-E.Fr.1132.51

μένω.definition: Ep. inf. Il.5.486; Arc. pres. part; lodge, stay, Pi.P.4.186; Hp.Ep.13; Plb.30.4.10 codd. , cf. Alciphr.3.5

μεραρχία.definition: command of a Ascl. l.c., Arr. l.c

μερίζω.definition: Dor. Bion2.31: Att. fut; assign a part, allot, Arist.MM1213b5; allot the interest according to the voyage, i.e. pay only a part of it, if a part only of the voyage has been performed, D.56.49; allot, assign spheres of…

μέριμνα.definition: care, thought, solicitude; concrete, object of care or thought, h.Merc.160

μερίς.definition: part, portion, Pl.Sph.266a; contribution, quota, contribute to . . , Id.21.70; . . ib.184; Plu.2.644c; Thphr.Char.17.2

μερίτης.definition: partaker, sharer; of a Lyd.Mag.3.70, Just.Nov.123.16 Intr

μερμηρίζω.definition: fut. Od.16.261: Ep. aor. (V; intr., to be anxious or thoughtful, to be in doubt: folld. by etc., was debating how he should . . , Il.2.3; . . , 14.159; Od.9.554: more freq. . . , . . debated anxiously whether . . , or…

μεσάζω.definition: Pass., to be inserted in the middle, intervene, A.D.Synt.270.5, cf. Conj.255.20; of terms in an arithmetical series, Theol.Ar.39

μέσαυλος.definition: in Hom. or , prob. the inner court, inside the where cattle were put at night, 11.11.548, 17.112,657, 24.29; used of the cave of the Cyclops, Od.10.435

μεσαύχην.definition: bound in the middle of the neck, comically for wine-skins , Ar.Fr.725

μεσεγγύη.definition: security by means of a third party, Gloss

μεσέγγυος.definition: third party, with whom a security is; deposit, IG7.3172.69

μεσεύω.definition: keep the middle or mean between two, c. gen; abs., stand midway, Arist.Pol.1327b29

μεσίτης.definition: mediator, umpire, arbitrator; fem. Luc.Am.27; ib.54

μεσοειδής.definition: in the region of the i.e. in the middle region of the voice, Aristid. Quint.1.12

μεσόζευγμα.definition: a word which belongs equally to what precedes and to what follows, Diom.p.444 K.; also Sacerd.p.456 K

μεσολαβέω.definition: seize, nip, Antyll. ap; perh. he shall calculate the size of the stones in proportion, BCH 20.324

μεσονεφής.definition: with clouds in the midst, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.138

μεσοταγής.definition: placed in the middle, Iamb.in Nic.p.84 P

μεσότομος.definition: poet. cut through the middle, split, AP6.63

μεσότυχος.definition: poet. of moderate fortune, Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod. Astr.1.109

μεσοφανής.definition: Ep. appearing in the; half-appearing, of the half-moon, ib.38.247

μεσόχορος.definition: standing in mid-chorus, of the; leader of a claque, Plin.Ep.2.14

μεσόχωρος.definition: midland, Gloss.; the middle space, Apollod.Poliorc.192.6

μεσπίλη.definition: medlar-tree, Mespilus germanica; oriental thorn, Crataegus orientalis, ibid

μέσπιλον.definition: medlar, Archil.180; azarole, Crataegus Azarolus, ibid. Archil. and Amphis ll. cc.; in Eub.74.4.]

μέστωσις.definition: filling full, saturation; in Lit. Crit., overcrowding with detail, Syrian.in Hermog.1.36R

μεσῳδός.definition: portion of a choral ode, coming between the strophe and antistrophe, without anything to correspond with it, Heph.Poëm.7.2

μεταβαίνω.definition: fut. h.Ven.293: aor; in writing or speaking, pass from one subject to another, change thy theme, Od.8.492; changing their course, turning round, Hdt.8.4; h.Ven.l.c.; Pl.Cra.438a; Id.Phdr.265c; Phld.Rh.1.172 S.; advanc…

μεταβολή.definition: change, changing; exchange, barter, with a view to traffic, Th.6.31: metaph., Epicur.Fr.479

μεταβουλεύω.definition: alter one's plans, change one's mind; mostly in Med., Hdt.1.156, E.Or.1526 ; Pl.Epin.982d; Hdt.8.57: c. et inf., Id.7.12: c. gen., repent of, Alciphr.2.4.19

μετάγω.definition: translate, LXXSi.Prol; derive a metaphor, Phld.Rh.1.179 S

μεταδαίνυμαι.definition: fut. , share the feast, Il.22.498, cf. Od.18.48; partake of, c. gen. rei, . . Il.23.207: abs., Q.S.2.157

μεταδόσιμον.definition: certificate, notice served; Adj. of disease, infectious, Archig. ap. Aët.13.120

μεταδότης.definition: one who imparts generously, Phld.Oec.p.53 J

μεταδρομή.definition: pursuit, chase, esp. of hounds; running to and fro, of hunted hares, Plu.2.971d

μεταθέω.definition: fut. run after, X.Cyn.6.22; pursue; hunt or range over, X.Cyn.4.9: abs., hunt about, range, ib.6.25,al

μεταΐζω.definition: poet. for seat oneself with or beside, Od.16.362

μεταίρω.definition: Aeol. lift up and; intr., depart, Ev.Matt.13.53, cf. 19.1

μεταΐσσω.definition: rush after, rush upon, Hom., always in pres; follow closely in another's steps, Pi.N.5.43. in Hom.]

μεταιτέω.definition: demand one's share of, c. gen. rei; abs., D.19.222, cf. Luc.Nec.17

μετακιάθω.definition: Ep. Verb, only impf. or aor; visit, Od.1.22, cf. Call.Dian.46; go to seek, A.R.3.802; simply, come to, Id.1.1221

μετακλαίω.definition: weep afterwards or too late; lament afterwards, Ph.1.209:—Med., E.Hec.214

μετακρούω.definition: push into another position : metaph., change one's opinion, v.l. in Plu.2.1069c

μεταλγής.definition: bringing sorrow in its train, prob. l., ib.111

μεταλήγω.definition: Ep. leave off, cease from, c. gen., Il.9.157, cf. h.Cer.339: abs., in Ep. impf. A.R.3.951

μεταλλάω.definition: search carefully, inquire diligently; c. acc. pers., inquire of, question, . . Il.1.553, cf. Od.3.69, 16.287; but . . the voice sought him out, Pi.O.6.62

μεταλλεία.definition: searching for metals and the like; mining operations in a siege, D.S.16.74

μεταπαύομαι.definition: rest between-whiles; c. gen., cease from, Opp.H.1.115

μεταπηδάω.definition: leap from one place to another, hop or; leap among, App.Hann.23

μεταπλέω.definition: change one's sailing, sail on another tack, An.Ox.3.219; Ion. Opp.H.3.427

μεταπρέπω.definition: distinguish oneself or be distinguished among, c. dat. pl., Il.2.481, etc.: freq. of heroes, ib.579; 13.175; 11.720, cf. Hes.Th.92 ; Phalaec. ap. Ath.10.440d; Orph.A.806: c. dat. modi, I am distinguished among the Tro…

μετασεύομαι.definition: Ep. aor. :—Pass., go; rush back, A.R.4.1270

μετασπάω.definition: draw over from one side to another, S.OC774

μεταστένω.definition: lament afterwards; Med., lament after or next, E.Med.996

μεταστρέφω.definition: turn round, retort, D.41.13; twist or turn all ways, Pl.Tht.191c; Id.Phdr.272b; turn upside down, Philem.111:—Pass., Men.5

μετατίθημι.definition: fut. fut. D.19.341; place among, then he would not have caused so much noise among us, Od.18.402

μεταυγάζω.definition: Dor. look keenly after, look; shine, glitter, Philostr.Im.1.19

μεταυδάω.definition: speak among, and so address, in Hom. always; later c. acc. pers., accost, address, ib.54, Mosch.4.61

μετάφημι.definition: speak among persons, whether in addressing one or more of them, or as their spokesman, Hom. , c. dat. pl., Od.18.312; Il.19.100: elsewh. Hom. always joins it with or whether a single person is addressed, as in Il.2.41…

μεταφράζω.definition: paraphrase, D.H.Th.45, TheonProg.1; translate, J.AJ8.5.3, Plu.Cat.Ma.19, Cic.40

μεταφωνέω.definition: speak among, only in impf. , c; c. acc. pers., accost, Id.1.702

μετεγχέω.definition: pour from one vessel into another, EM149.41

μέτειμι.definition: to be among, c. dat. pl; impers., I have a share in or claim to a thing, Hdt.1.171, etc.; A.Eu.575; S.OT630, cf. Ant.1072, Ar.Av.1666, 1668; Arist.Pol.1292a3: so part. neut. used abs., since they had no more share in …

μετέρχομαι.definition: Aeol. and Dor. Pi.N.7.74; go among with hostile purpose, attack, 16.487: with a double construction, Od.6.132

μετοικέτης.definition: one who dwells in the middle, Id

μετοικίζω.definition: lead settlers to another abode; later intr. in Act., SIG880.45

μετοίχομαι.definition: go after, go in quest of; with hostile intent, rush upon, pursue, Il.5.148

μετοκλάζω.definition: keep changing from one leg to the other, of a coward squatting in ambush, Il.13.281: metaph., D.S.38/9.13; of a bird, AP9.209

μετουσία.definition: participation, partnership, communion; in Philos., = participation in the universal by the particular, Polyxenus ap.Alex.Aphr.in Metaph.84.18; Plot.6.1.9, cf. 5.3.15, Procl.in Prm.p.557 S

μετοχή.definition: sharing, participation, Hdt.1.144; Astrol., joint possession or occupation by two planets, Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.107, 115, Porph.in Ptol.190

μετοχλίζω.definition: remove by a lever, hoist a heavy body out of the way, . . , Od.23.188; would he easily push back the bolt of the doors, Il.24.567, cf. Lyc.627, AP9.81 ; Philostr.Im.2.21

μετρέω.definition: Heraclean I pl. impf; of Space, measure, i. e. pass over, traverse, Od.3.179; to sail farther, A.R.2.915, cf. 4.1779:—in Med., Mosch.2.157; measuring them with the eyes, S.Aj.5:—Pass., to be measured, A.Ch.209; to be …

μετριάζω.definition: to be moderate, keep measure, S.Ph.1183; of disease, remit, abate, opp. Gal.16.711

μηδέπω.definition: Adv. nor as yet, not as yet, Id.Pr.741, Pers.435, etc

μήδομαι.definition: Il.2.360, etc.: impf. h.Merc.46; Ep; c. acc. rei, plan and do cunningly or skilfully, plot, contrive, in Ep. mostly in bad sense, Il.7.478; Od.24.96; 3.194; Hes.Sc.34; Id.Fr.96.85: also c. acc. pers. et rei, he wrough…

μηκάς.definition: bleating one, in Hom. always of goats; as Subst., = S.Fr.509, AP9.123 ; Luc.DDMeretr.7.1: pl., Theoc.1.87, 5.100

μηκωνίς.definition: Dor. wild lettuce; a form of spurge, Hp.Int.7

μηλόω.definition: probe a wound, Hp.Morb.1.6; in Med., dye wool, Eust.1394.33

μηνίω.definition: Dor. fut. AP9.79 , LXXJe.3.12, al.: aor. :—cherish wrath, be wroth against, c. dat. pers., Il.1.422; 18.257; cf. 5.84, 7.229: c. gen. rei, because of . . , Il.5.178; S.Ant.1177; Id.Tr.274; . . Id.OC965: c. acc. cogn.,…

μηνυτήρ.definition: informer, guide, A.Eu.245; one who shows, reveals, Orph.H.41.7

μηρίζω.definition: strike on the thigh, Com. word coined on analogy of D.L.7.172

μήρυμα.definition: that which is drawn out: strand of; a serpent's coil or trail, Nic.Th.160, 265

μηρύομαι.definition: Dor. Theoc. : aor; in weaving, weave the woof into the warp, Hes.Op.538

μητίομαι.definition: Pi.P.2.92 : fut. aor. — = II, devise, contrive, Il.3.416; 10.48; Od.12.373; Il.15.349; Emp.139; Parm.13; . . A.R.3.1026: c. dupl.acc., Od.18.27. in fut. and aor., and late Act. Orph.A.1333; in Pi.l.c.]

μητρίζω.definition: to be possessed by the Mother of the gods, Iamb.Myst.3.9, 10

μητρογάμος.definition: one guilty of such incest, Arg.Man.post Max.p.98 L

μητρόληπτος.definition: possessed by the Mother of the gods, Herm.in Phdr.p.105 A

μηχανάομαι.definition: more freq. contrive, devise, by art or cunning, freq. in bad sense, Od.3.207, 17.499, 22.432; Antipho1.3; but in good sense, X.Cyr.2.2.12; Pl.Prt.320e; simply, bring about, effect, Hdt.2.21; X.Cyr.1.6.22:—Constr.: con…

μιαίνω.definition: fut. Antipho2.2.11; 3sg; freq. of moral pollution, taint, defile, Pi. l. c., etc.; Sol.l. c., E.Hel. l. c.; S.Fr.104; App.BC2.104; A.Ag.637; Id.Th.344 ; Id.Ag.1669; Pl.Lg.868b, Ti.69d; Porph.Abst.4.12; S.Ant.1044; Ant…

μικρώνυμος.definition: in Comp., named by a smaller number, Iamb.in Nic.p.71 P

μιλιάζω.definition: measure by miles and mark by milestones, in Pass., Plb.34.11.8

μίλτειος.definition: of the red mark made by the carpenter's line, ib.6.103

μίλφωσις.definition: falling off of the eyelashes, ib.789

μίμαυλος.definition: mimic actor, accompanied on the flute, Ath.10.452f

μίμημα.definition: anything imitated, counterfeit; artistic representation, Pl.Lg.669e, 796b

μιμνάζω.definition: Ep. form of wait, stay, Il.2.392; trans., await, expect, c. acc., h.Hom.9.6

μιμνήσκω.definition: fut. aor. causal Verb, formed in pres. and impf. from as from put in mind, Od.12.38; of a thing, 3.103; Il.15.31, cf. 1.407; Od.14.169, cf. Thgn.1123, Theoc.15.36. II. . . recalled it to memory, made it famous, Pi.P.1…

μίμνω.definition: Poet. redupl. pres. and impf. of; tarry, 6.69, etc

μινύθω.definition: only pres. and Ion. impf; diminish in number, Od.14.17

μινυρίζω.definition: mostly pres. and impf.: aor. 1, Plu.2.56f; sing in a low tone, warble, hum, Ar.Av.1414, Pl.R.411a; Ar.V.219; opp. Arist.HA618b31; of the voice of the ib.619a3

μιξόπυος.definition: mixed with foul matter, Hp.Epid.1.10, Ruf.Ren.Ves.2.6

μισέω.definition: pf. Pl.Phlb.44c:—Pass., fut. Med. in pass. sense E.Tr.664, Ion597, 611, Philostr.VA6.13, later LXXSi.21.28, Aristid.2.426 J., D.C.52.39: aor. Hdt.2.119, etc.: pf. Isoc.5.137, Hdn.8.5.8: :—hate, once in Hom., c. acc. e…

μισήλιος.definition: hating the sun or light, Gloss

μιστύλλω.definition: cut up, in Hom. always of cutting up meat before roasting, Il.1.465, cf. 9.210, al.; Od.14.75; metaph., of a sun-dial, AP9.782 : pres. part., Ar.Fr.409, Clidem.17: aor. 1 Semon.24: part. fem. Lyc.154: Med. Nonn.D.21.115

μιτόομαι.definition: Med., ply the woof in weaving, AP6.285 : metaph., let one's voice sound like a string, ib.7.195 ; also, of Fate, IG12.1240.15

μνάομαι.definition: contr. used by Hom. sts; to be mindful of, c. gen., Il.2.686; 11.71; Call.Ap.95: abs., when I remember him, Od.4.106, cf. 15.400; also, turn one's mind to a thing, Il.16.697

μνηστεύω.definition: promise in marriage, betroth, E.El.313; to bring about a marriage for another, help him to a wife, Call.Dian.265, A.R.2.511:—Pass., his betrothed wife, Ev.Luc.2.5

μογέω.definition: in Trag., suffer pain, be distressed, A.Pr.277; Id.Ag.1624; in the side, E.Alc.849: c. dat., Call.Del.242 ; Nic.Th.830: metaph., having lost its sheen, Id.Al.529

μοιράω.definition: share, divide, distribute; Med., divided, i. e. tore their hair, A.R.4.1533

μοιχεύω.definition: commit adultery with a woman, debauch her, c; metaph., worship idolatrously, LXXJe.3.9

μοιχή.definition: rare form for Ar.Byz. ap. Eust.1761.24

μοιχίς.definition: rare fem. of Ar.Byz. ap. Eust.1761.24

μολπῆτις.definition: Dor. she who sings and dances, metaph., AP6.288

μολυβδίζω.definition: to be leaden in colour, Olymp.Alch.p.71 B

μολύβδωσις.definition: leading or soldering with lead, Gloss

μοναρχέω.definition: Ion. to be sovereign; hold the office of at Cos, SIG805.6, Sor.Vit. Hippocr

μόναρχος.definition: Ion. monarch, sole ruler; princelet, dynast, OGI54.16 : generally, leader, general, E.Rh.31

μοναυλέω.definition: play a solo on the flute, Plu.Caes.52

μονοβάμων.definition: gen. walking alone; metre of but one foot, Simm.26.9

μονογαμέω.definition: to be the husband of one wife, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.209

μονοδοξέω.definition: possess fame alone, Simp.in Epict.p.86 D

μονόκοκκος.definition: with a single grain, of pearls, Gloss.; also of onions, ibid

μονόκρουνον.definition: jug with a single spout, Haussoullier Milet p.199

μονόκωπος.definition: with one oar: poet., with one ship, E.Hel.1128

μονόλινον.definition: necklace of a single string of pearls, Capitolin.Vit. Maximini Jun.1.8

μονόλυκος.definition: solitary, i. e. singularly fierce; as Adj., Arat.1124 [with 2nd syll. long]

μονομερής.definition: consisting of one part, single; for one side, of a bandage, Gal.18 .794

μονοπάλης.definition: Ion. one who conquers in wrestling only , Epigr. ap. Paus.6.4.6

μονόφθογγος.definition: monophthong, single vowel, opp. Theodos.Can.p.68 H

μονόφρων.definition: gen. single in one's opinion, ib.757

μονόφωνος.definition: with but one voice or tone, of deaf- mutes, Hp.Carn.18

μονόω.definition: Ep. and Ion. Od.16.117, Hdt; more freq. in Pass., to be left alone, forsaken, Il. l. c.; Od.15.386; they were left each man by himself, Hdt.8.123; taken apart, without witnesses , Id.1.116; A.Supp.749; of animals when…

μονῳδία.definition: monody, solo, opp. the song of the chorus; monody, lament, Him.Or.23.1: pl., ib.8

μορέω.definition: make with pain and toil, . . Dosiad.Ara8, cf. EM584.31 ; i. e. boiled over a fire, Nic.Al.229 , q. v.)

μορμύρω.definition: of water, roar and boil; metaph., Man.5.118

μορύσσω.definition: Ep. Verb, = soil, defile, in pf. part

μορφάζω.definition: gesticulate, X.Smp.6.4; make grimaces, Phld.Vit.p.38 J., cf. Ael.NA1.29

μόρφωσις.definition: shaping, bringing into shape; form, semblance, Ep.Rom.2.20, 2 Ep.Ti.3.5

μορφώτρια.definition: fem. as if from changing men into swine, E.Tr.437

μοσχεύω.definition: plant a sucker, Thphr.CP1.2.1, 3.5.1, etc; train as a calf, Philostr.VA6.30

μοσχοτόμος.definition: slaughtering calves, i.e. sacrificer, Lat. victimarius, Gloss

μοτός.definition: tent, tampon, lint pledget for dressing; drainage tube, Hp.Morb.2.47; also ib.59

μοτώ.definition: a kind of cinnamon, Peripl.M.Rubr.12,13, Gal.14.72

μούλη.definition: = Lat. mula, mule, PMag. Lond.121.927, PLips.97 xxi 20 , Alex.Trall.1.15

μουσόπνοος.definition: contr. breathing melody, of Hesiod, Anon. ap. Procl.Proll. Hes.p.4 G

μουσόω.definition: furnish with power of song; adorn with mosaic, Ath.Mitt.8.328

μοχθέω.definition: to be weary or worn with toil, to be sore; c. acc. objecti, . . the children over whom I toiled, E.HF281; = Id.Ph.1549

μοχθίζω.definition: = toil for money, Pi.Fr.123.6; . . suffering from the wound . . , Il.2.723; Thgn.164; Archil.137; Theoc.1.38, 7.48; Mosch.4.44: abs., Orph.A.1071

μόχλευσις.definition: moving by a lever, setting joints; removal, dislodgement, extirpation, Aret.CD1.2

μοχλευτής.definition: one who heaves by a lever: hence Com. he who makes earth and sea to heave, Ar.Nu.567; . . O thou who heavest up new words, ib.1397

μοχλέω.definition: Ion. for foreg., they strove to heave them up with levers, Il.12.259

μυδάω.definition: to be damp, dripping; to be damp, clammy from decay, Hp.VC15; of a corpse, S.Ant.410

μυέω.definition: initiate into the mysteries; generally, teach, instruct, c. inf., AP7.385 ; ib.9.162:—Pass., Ep.Phil.4.12; Alciphr.2.4.21

μυθέομαι.definition: Ep. 2sg. Od.8.180; speak, abs., Il.7.76, 8.40, etc.; Semon.7.18; converse, A.R.1.458: c. acc. et inf., say that . . , Il.21.462: c. inf., order, A.Pr.664, prob. in Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19: c. acc., tell, recount, Il.…

μυθηγορέω.definition: tell stories, in Pass., Procl.Proll.Hes.p.5 G

μυθολογεύω.definition: tell word for word, Od.12.450; ib.453: generally, relate, Ps.-Phoc.68, prob. rest. in Sapph.Supp.7.4

μυθολόγος.definition: teller of legends, romancer, joined; Adj. mythological, Call.Aet.3.1.55

μυθῳδός.definition: singer of mythic tales, cj. for in Cat.Cod.Astr.8.211

μυκάομαι.definition: of things, Il.5.749; 12.460; of a shield, rang, 20.260; of meat, bellowed upon the spits , Od.12.395; Hes.Op.508; Ar.Nu.292; Theoc.22.75:—rare in Prose, Pl.R.396b, 615e, Arist.Mete.368a25.—An aor. Act., AP6.220.11

μυκητίας σεισμός.definition: an earthquake accompanied with roaring underground, Arist.Mu.396a11

μύλαξ.definition: millstone, any large round stone, Il.12.161, AP9.418 , 546 , Opp.C.3.137

μυλάριον.definition: Dim. of I, of a spell used in grinding salt, PMag.Par.1.3087

μύλη.definition: mill: in Hom., hand-mill turned by women; nether millstone , Ar.V.648: pl., Arist.Mete.383b7, cf. Pherecr.10

μυλιάω.definition: gnash or grind the teeth, only in Ep. part., , Hes.Op.530

μυλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be hardened, cicatrized, of wounds, f.l. for in Hp.Mul.1.40, as read by Erot. is prob. cj. for in Hp.Coac.501

μυξόρροος.definition: running at the nose, Hp.Morb.Sacr.5, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.20.17

μυουρίζω.definition: of the pulse, die away gradually, Ruf.Syn.Puls.8.1, Gal.8.480, 524, 9.322

μυρίζω.definition: rub with ointment or unguent, anoint; in Pass. also, to be fragrant with . . , Hld.10.26

μυριόπους.definition: gen. ten-thousand-; having sides ten thousand feet long, Thphr.CP6.2.4

μυρμηκίας λίθος.definition: a precious stone with wart-like; glod dug by II, Hld.10.26

μυρμηκίζω.definition: feel as though ants were running under the; have a feeling of irritation, itch, Aët.12.48

μυροπόλος.definition: or busy about scented oils or, selling unguents, alternative forms in EM595.31

μύρω.definition: Ep. Verb, Act. only impf., flow, trickle; elsewh. always in Med. , melt into tears, shed tears, Il.19.6; 22.427; 6.373, cf. Od.19.119; Hes.Op.206: aor. 1 opt. 2sg. Theoc.16.31

μύρωμα.definition: ointment spread for use, Ar.Ec.1117, cf. Eust.1295.20

μυσπολέω.definition: run about like a mouse, Ar.V.140, with a play on

μύσσομαι.definition: fut. Epic.in Arch.Pap.7.5:—blow the nose, Hp.Vict.3.70:—Act. is only found in compds. ; Skt. muncáti 'let go', Lat. e-mungo.)

μύω.definition: fut. Lyc.988: aor. Ep. 3pl; intr., close, be shut, of the eyes, Il.24.637; from closed eye, E.l.c.; of the mouth or any opening, Pl.Phdr.251d; AP7.630 ; ib.15.40 ; . . ib.10.5 ; of bivalve fish, opp. Ath.3.93f; of flo…

μυωνιά.definition: prob. = as a term of reproach for a lewd woman, Epicr.9.4

μυωπάζω.definition: blink the eyes, as shortsighted persons do : hence, to be shortsighted, metaph., 2 Ep.Pet.1.9

μῶ.definition: = coined as etym. of many words, EM84.47, al; = I, Democr.19, BCH29.483

μωλύω.definition: or boil imperfectly, parboil, scald; of ulcers, 'go off the boil', fail to come to a head, subside, fade away, Hp.Epid.7.3 ; ib.2.2.6 .328); Hp. ap. Gal.19.124; · Gal.19.121; of certain diseases, latent and 'simmering…

μωλωπίζω.definition: beat and bruise severely; resemble mosquito bites, Herod.Med. ap. Aët.5.129

μῶμαι.definition: Med., 3sg. Epich.117; 3pl; meditate or purpose, c. acc., S. ll.cc

μωμάομαι.definition: Ion. 3pl. Thgn.369, cf. 169; inf. Hp.de Arte1: fut. Il.3.412, Thgn.1079; Dor. Simon.5.5: aor. A.Ag.277; Dor. poet. Theoc.9.24: :—find fault with, blame, criticize, c. acc., Il. l.c., Thgn.169, 369, Simon. l.c., A. l.c…

μωροβλάπτης.definition: pestilent fool, Anon. in Script.Physiogn. ii p.126 Foerster

μά.definition: Particle used in asseverations and oaths; in affirmation, yea by this staff, Il.1.234, cf. h.Merc.460; Pi.N.11.24; etc., Ar.Ach.88, Pl.R.407b, etc.; also Inscr.Cypr.109 H

μακράν.definition: Ion. acc. fem. of used as Adv

μέγαρόνδε.definition: Adv. to the hall, to the women's room, Od.16.413, al

μέν.definition: Particle, used partly to express certainty on the; used absolutely to express certainty, not followed by correlative indeed, of a truth, synonymous with as appears from the Ep. and Ion. form in protestations and oaths…

μέχρι.definition: and Adv. as far as, so used chiefly in; Prep. c. gen., even to, as far as

μέχριπερ.definition: or Conj., so long as; until, Luc.Cyn.13

μηδέ.definition: in . . . . the first may belong to A, e.g. Il.4.303 sq., or to B, e.g. Pl.R.391c; . . Pi.I.2.45, Pl.Prt.327d; but cannot follow after v. A.II.3. B. as Adv., joined with a single word or phrase, not even, not either, I…

μηδόλως.definition: Adv., for not at all, Cerc.f17.21, Gal.Protr.1, etc

μίγα.definition: Adv. mixed, blent with, Pi.P.4.113; A.R.4.1345; together with . . , Epigr.Gr.386

μίγδα.definition: Adv. promiscuously, confusedly, Od.24.77, h.Cer.426, Alc.70: c. dat., among the gods, Il.8.437

μοναχῆ.definition: Adv., prop. dat. sg. fem. of in one way only, opp. Pl.Lg.720e, etc.; in which way only, X.An.4.4.18

μοναχῶς.definition: Adv. in one way only, opp; in a uniform way, Id.HA584a34

μονικῶς.definition: Adv., dub. sens. in Phld.Hom.p.14 O

μουνάξ.definition: Adv., singly, Od.8.371; in single combat, 11.417

μυχόθεν.definition: Adv. from the inmost part of the house, from the women's chambers, A.Ag.96 , Ch.35

μυχόνδε.definition: Adv. to the far corner, ib.22.270; inwards, Emp.100.23
